pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Taking of Christ — the armed men laying hold of Christ in the torchlight and closing their hands on Him, to the tune of A Dove on Distant Oaks a Miktam of David when the Philistines seized him in Gath, be merciful to me O God
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_taking_of_christ

pictures.scene: Frans Snyders, The Boar Hunt — the pack of hounds fastened onto the boar and driving it down, for men are hounding me, all day they press their attack
pictures.name: pd_snyders_the_boar_hunt

pictures.scene: Alfred Wierusz-Kowalski, A Sleigh Chased by Wolves — the wolves running flat out behind the sleigh over the open snow, my enemies pursue me all day long, for many proudly assail me
pictures.name: pd_wierusz_kowalski_troika_chased_by_wolves

pictures.scene: Andrea Mantegna, The Agony in the Garden — Christ on His knees on the bare rock with the soldiers already coming up the road, when I am afraid, I put my trust in You
pictures.name: pd_mantegna_the_agony_in_the_garden

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Moses with the Tablets of the Law — the prophet holding the written word of God up over his head in both hands, in God whose word I praise, in God I trust
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_moses_with_the_tablets_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Anton von Werner, Luther at the Diet of Worms — the one man standing up before the whole assembly and refusing to take back a word of it, I will not be afraid, what can man do to me
pictures.name: pd_von_werner_luther_at_the_diet_of_worms

pictures.scene: Gerard van Honthorst, Christ before the High Priest — the accuser leaning across the table with his finger on the book while Christ stands silent, all day long they twist my words, all their thoughts are on my demise
pictures.name: pd_honthorst_christ_before_the_high_priest

pictures.scene: Georges de La Tour, The Denial of Saint Peter — the soldiers bent over their game in the candlelight, waiting and watching in the courtyard, they conspire they lurk, they watch my steps
pictures.name: pd_la_tour_the_denial_of_saint_peter

pictures.scene: Vasily Surikov, The Morning of the Streltsy Execution — the condemned men held in the square with their candles while the guards wait to take them, while they wait to take my life, in spite of such sin will they escape
pictures.name: pd_surikov_the_morning_of_the_streltsy_execution

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Tower of Babel — the huge tower of the nations already cracking and sinking under its own weight, in Your anger O God cast down the nations
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Titian, Mater Dolorosa — the mother with the tears still standing on her face and her hands open before her, You have taken account of my wanderings, put my tears in Your bottle
pictures.name: pd_titian_mater_dolorosa

pictures.scene: Cornelis Claesz van Wieringen, The Explosion of the Spanish Flagship — the enemy ship blown apart and the rest of the fleet turning away from it, are they not in Your book, then my enemies will retreat
pictures.name: pd_van_wieringen_the_explosion_of_the_spanish_flagship

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint George and the Dragon — the rider driving his lance into the dragon as the girl who called for help looks back, on the day I cry for help, by this I will know that God is on my side
pictures.name: pd_raphael_saint_george_and_the_dragon

pictures.scene: Antonello da Messina, Saint Jerome in his Study — the scholar alone at his desk with the great book open under his hands, in the LORD whose word I praise, in God I trust I will not be afraid
pictures.name: pd_antonello_saint_jerome_in_his_study

pictures.scene: Nikolai Ge, What is Truth — Christ standing bound and silent in the corner while the governor who can kill Him argues with his hand out, what can man do to me, Your vows are upon me O God
pictures.name: pd_ge_what_is_truth

pictures.scene: Jan Steen, Prayer Before the Meal — the household stopped with folded hands over the bread before anyone touches it, I will render thank offerings to You, for You have delivered my soul from death
pictures.name: pd_steen_prayer_before_the_meal

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Wanderer above the Sea of Fog — the traveler standing firm on the rock above the cloud with his staff set down beside him, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_wanderer_above_the_sea_of_fog

pictures.scene: William Holman Hunt, The Light of the World — Christ carrying the lit lantern through the dark and knocking at the overgrown door, in the light of life
pictures.name: pd_hunt_the_light_of_the_world

lines.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “A Dove on Distant Oaks.” A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.
Be merciful to me, O God,
for men are hounding me;
all day they press their attack.
My enemies pursue me all day long,
for many proudly assail me.
When I am afraid,
I put my trust in You.
In God, whose word I praise—
in God I trust.
I will not be afraid.
What can man do to me?
All day long they twist my words;
all their thoughts are on my demise.
They conspire, they lurk,
they watch my steps
while they wait to take my life.
In spite of such sin, will they escape?
In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations.
You have taken account of my wanderings.
Put my tears in Your bottle—
are they not in Your book?
Then my enemies will retreat
on the day I cry for help.
By this I will know that God is on my side.
In God, whose word I praise,
in the LORD, whose word I praise,
in God I trust; I will not be afraid.
What can man do to me?
Your vows are upon me, O God;
I will render thank offerings to You.
For You have delivered my soul from death,
and my feet from stumbling,
that I may walk before God
in the light of life.
